The `package()` function is not executed under these flags and thus not relevant for this safety gate.

The use of `SKIP` in checksums is not present here, and even if it were, it would not make this phase unsafe—only unverified. There is no evidence of exfiltration, dynamic payload fetching, obfuscated code, or execution of remote scripts during the sourcing or source-fetching phase. All operations within scope for this gate are safe and consistent with standard AUR packaging practices.

</details>

<security_assessment>

<details>

The script uses standard system libraries and subprocess calls to `clang-offload-bundler` and a tool `rj_pretranslate`, both of which are expected components in a ROCm development environment. It locates these tools in standard ROCm paths or via PATH, which is normal packaging behavior. All file operations are confined to reading input files and writing temporary translation artifacts, with no network activity, data exfiltration, or execution of externally fetched code.

The script interacts with ROCm-specific binaries and libraries (e.g., `librocm_kpack.so.0`) using ctypes and subprocess in a transparent and documented manner. It includes robust error handling and reporting but does not perform any privileged or suspicious operations. The functionality aligns with performance optimization in containerized environments, a legitimate use case.
</details>
